quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (management): non-GAAP earnings of $4.76 per share for full year 2025 versus $4.57 in 2024, delivering on the revised 2025 guidance range of $4.72 to $4.80; GAAP EPS of $4.05 versus $2.27 in 2024, including a net loss of $75,000,000, or $0.20 per share, for an increased liability for expected future obligations to Global Infrastructure Partners from the 09/30/2024 sale of the South Fork Wind and Revolution Wind projects. Q4 GAAP and non-GAAP EPS were both $1.12 versus $1.01 non-GAAP a year earlier. Electric distribution earned $1.80 per share (vs $1.77), mainly on Massachusetts and New Hampshire base distribution rate increases; natural gas distribution earned $0.97 (vs $0.81). The electric transmission segment is transcribed as $2.09 per share in 2025 versus $2.30 in 2024, yet the speaker calls these 'improved results' driven by 'continued investments in our electric transmission system to address service reliability and demand growth', so the pair does not match the speaker's own description and is kept out of the figure. Dividends paid were $3.01 per share, a 5.2% increase.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 non-GAAP EPS $4.76 (vs $4.57 in 2024); GAAP EPS $4.05 (vs $2.27); Q4 GAAP and non-GAAP EPS $1.12 (vs Q4 2024 non-GAAP $1.01); electric distribution $1.80 per share (vs $1.77); natural gas distribution $0.97 per share (vs $0.81); dividends $3.01 per share, a 5.2% increase

quarterly_data.signal: Initial 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance (management) of $4.80 to $4.95 per share; it does not assume the Aquarion sale and includes water segment earnings (a point-in-time range, revised later in 2026 per the newer Eversource entries). 2026 growth is expected to be more moderate due to the timing of key regulatory outcomes (the potential Aquarion sale and storm cost recovery in Connecticut and New Hampshire), which management calls transitory. Positive 2026 drivers: 'transmission investments to improve system resiliency and to address increased electric demand', PBR distribution rate increases in Massachusetts and now New Hampshire (the NSTAR Electric PBR adjustment of $55,000,000 was implemented January 1), and O&M management; offsets are higher depreciation and property taxes, higher interest costs, share dilution and a higher effective tax rate. Management expects a 'meaningful inflection in earnings growth' in 2027 and 2028: the CL&P rate case to be filed midyear 2026 with a rate adjustment midyear 2027, and Connecticut storm cost securitization around 2027 (PURA prudency decision expected by July, cash in the door around the Q3 timeframe of 2027). Long-term EPS growth of 5% to 7% is based off 2025 non-GAAP recurring EPS of $4.76, with growth towards the upper half by 2028 measured off 2027 earnings, which the CFO said 'implies over 6%'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 EPS guidance $4.80 to $4.95 (initial, assumes no Aquarion sale); long-term EPS growth 5% to 7% off 2025 non-GAAP $4.76; upper half by 2028, implies over 6% off 2027 earnings

quarterly_data.signal: New five-year capital plan for 2026 through 2030 of approximately $26,500,000,000 in the regulated electric and natural gas businesses (only projects with a clear line of sight on regulatory approval), a $2,300,000,000 increase over the prior five-year plan and a $1,500,000,000 increase for the overlapping 2026 through 2029 period; Aquarion Water would add $1,300,000,000 and is excluded. Electric distribution is the largest driver of the increase at $696,000,000, with over $11,000,000,000 of electric distribution investment driven primarily by the Massachusetts Electric Sector Modernization Plan and over $300,000,000 remaining for the Massachusetts AMI program. Natural gas distribution adds $523,000,000 (nearly $7,000,000,000 in total; newly effective mandatory safety regulations are approximately 25% of the growth in the gas plan). Transmission rises $233,000,000 for the overlapping period, with over $7,000,000,000 of transmission investment over the five years, covering replacement of aging infrastructure to harden the system and 'innovative substation and other infrastructure projects undertaken for reliability and load growth'. Technology and facilities rise $75,000,000 to $1,200,000,000, including cybersecurity investments and AI tools. This is the transmission, substation and distribution spend behind the utility's grid equipment demand; the plan total and segment totals as filed are in the Eversource 10-K entry.
quarterly_data.figure: +$1,500,000,000 for the overlapping 2026 through 2029 period: electric distribution +$696,000,000, natural gas distribution +$523,000,000, transmission +$233,000,000, technology and facilities +$75,000,000 (now $1,200,000,000); Aquarion (excluded) would add $1,300,000,000 over the five years

quarterly_data.signal: Transmission and rate base (management): the transmission capital plan includes future ESMIP (as transcribed) substations towards the end of the five-year forecast period; for that reason and to address load growth for the New England region, the plan carries sizable transmission investments for NSTAR Electric, which will have the largest transmission rate base in the service territory, projected at nearly $8,000,000,000 by 2030. The customer-focused core business investments in the capital plan result in 8.3% growth in rate base from 2024 through 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: NSTAR Electric transmission rate base nearly $8,000,000,000 by 2030; rate base growth 8.3% from 2024 through 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Substation build (CEO): in January 2025 Eversource broke ground on the Cambridge underground substation, a $1,800,000,000 investment described as 'the largest underground substation in the nation', strengthening the electric system that serves 'one of the fastest-growing and most energy-intensive areas of our region'; construction 'continues to progress very well'.
quarterly_data.figure: $1,800,000,000 Cambridge underground substation; ground broken January 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced metering (AMI): the Massachusetts program has reached over 100,000 smart meter installations in a multiyear effort to upgrade more than 1,500,000 meters statewide, with over $300,000,000 remaining for the program in the capital plan; the CEO said 'It is going very, very well.' Connecticut AMI stays outside the new plan: an analyst cited a billion dollars of upside tied to it, and management said 'that billion dollars that we have on the slide' should be viewed 'as a placeholder' because the number from a cost perspective 'is kind of stale'; a revised cost estimate will be filed. Eversource wants a waiver of the prudence standard and an updated implementation schedule (a Connecticut meeting was set for the following week) and will not make the investment 'until we feel comfortable with the recovery mechanism.'
quarterly_data.figure: over 100,000 smart meter installations in Massachusetts of more than 1,500,000 meters statewide; over $300,000,000 remaining for the Massachusetts AMI program

quarterly_data.signal: New England generation: Eversource completed construction of the onshore substation for the Revolution Wind project late last year. Citing Ørsted, the project was expected to achieve first power within the coming weeks, construction had resumed after a preliminary injunction on the stop work order, and the project was 87% complete. Commercial operation is targeted for the second half of 2026; COD, not first power, is the trigger that ends Eversource's exposure, and the contingent liability recorded in 2025 did not need to change. Management clarified: 'we do not have any liability to Ørsted. Our obligation is to GIP'. Ørsted leads disclosure on the project.
quarterly_data.figure: Revolution Wind 87% complete; first power expected within weeks; COD targeted second half of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Five-year funding plan (management): $27,800,000,000 of infrastructure investment including Aquarion plus dividends of $6,700,000,000 to $7,200,000,000 make a total cash need of $34,500,000,000 to $35,000,000,000. Cash flow from operations of $24,200,000,000 to $24,700,000,000 funds nearly 70%; approximately $8,500,000,000 to $9,000,000,000 comes from incremental debt and other financing (junior subordinated notes, a minority interest sale or minority-like capital structure transactions, with equity content of $1,300,000,000 to $2,500,000,000); storm cost securitization proceeds of up to $1,500,000,000 depend on the PURA prudency decision (98% of the $2,000,000,000 of deferred storm costs is in current rates or pending prudence reviews); and common equity issuance is roughly $800,000,000 to $1,100,000,000, unaffected by the Aquarion sale. An Aquarion sale would instead reduce the alternative financing (the Aquarion transaction was assumed to bring $1,600,000,000 from the equity portion of the sale), and Eversource expects to issue junior subordinated debt with or without Aquarion. FFO-to-debt improved by over 400 basis points at Moody's and 300 basis points at S&P in 2025, and the plan keeps at least a 100 basis point cushion over the downgrade thresholds. Roughly $500,000,000 of tax credits tied to tax equity ownership remain unused, keeping Eversource essentially a noncash federal taxpayer for several years.
quarterly_data.figure: total cash need $34,500,000,000 to $35,000,000,000; operating cash flow $24,200,000,000 to $24,700,000,000 (nearly 70%); incremental debt and other financing $8,500,000,000 to $9,000,000,000; securitization proceeds up to $1,500,000,000
